title: What If You Turned INVISIBLE?
description:
Glint, 19, works nights at the city science museum. During a storm, lightning hits a giant glass lens, and the light stops bouncing off him. He turns invisible... all except two tiny dark dots where his eyes should be. Then, on the third night, Nan collapses in the pitch-dark museum basement, the paramedics are lost in a maze of four floors, and nobody can see the one person who knows the way. He has ninety seconds, and one trick from real science: the red-eye effect.

Would you want to be invisible, knowing the people you love could never see your face? Tell me in the comments 👇

▶ More What Ifs: What If You Could Smell Like a Dog?

SOURCES
• Purves et al., Neuroscience (Sinauer): phototransduction. The retina must absorb light to see, so a truly invisible eye would be blind (a classic critique of H. G. Wells's The Invisible Man, 1897)
• Hecht, Optics (5th ed.): refraction and refractive index; why transparent things are still visible
• Proske & Gandevia, "The proprioceptive senses," Physiological Reviews 92 (2012)
• American Academy of Ophthalmology, "Red eye in photos" (aao.org)
• NASA Science, "Infrared Waves" (science.nasa.gov): humans give off infrared light
• Taboada et al., "Glassfrogs conceal blood in their liver to maintain transparency," Science 378 (2022)
• Fiction: the lens, the storm, the visible eyes and "anything he holds turns invisible" are rules of this story's world
